The error code for “(\mathbf{x} = \error)” used to be ( \mathtt{OOB}, \mathbf{e} ); now it becomes ( \panic, \registers_7, \mathbf{e} ). So the code is different: if we can’t parse the data to export, we do a panic instead of an OOB code.
The “import” host call has become a more general “fetch” that can read from multiple data sources within the work-package or the array of import segments.
The “historical lookup” call now references w_s from the new structure, plus (p_\mathbf{x})_t.

The function “F” (the host callback) used to handle calls to \Omega_Y(\dots, \mathbf{i}) under \mathtt{import}, but now the import call is replaced by \mathtt{fetch} that calls \Omega_Y(\dots, i, p, \mathbf{o}, \overline{\mathbf{i}}).

- Old call: 
 $\Psi_M(\Lambda(\delta[s], \mathbf{c}_t, c), 0, g, a, F, (\emptyset, []))$ 

- New call: 
 $\Psi_M(\Lambda(\delta[w_s], (p_\mathbf{x})_t, w_c), 0, w_g, a, F, (\emptyset, []))$

Moved from “(code-hash c, gas g, service index s, package hash p, payload \mathbf{y}, context \mathbf{c}, authorizer a, output \mathbf{o}, import segments \mathbf{i}, extrinsic data \overline{\mathbf{x}}, offset \segoff )” to a drastically simpler signature referencing “(work-item index i, the full work-package p, the output \mathbf{o}, the collective import data \overline{\mathbf{i}}, and offset \segoff).”
The new text explicitly defines \overline{\mathbf{i}} as an array of import-segment data for each work-item.
The refine function’s signature changes from a many-argument variant to one taking (j, \wpX, \mathbf{o}, \overline{\mathbf{i}}, \ell).
Shifted emphasis to clarify that \importsegmentdata and \extrinsicdata are separate.

Old text:
“It explicitly accepts the work payload, \mathbf{y}, the service index s, code-hash c, etc.”
New text:
“It explicitly accepts the work-package p and the index of the work item i…”

The descriptive text changed from “The return value for when a memory index is provided for reading/writing which is not accessible” to a slightly reworded statement focusing on “the inner \textsc{pvm} memory index.”
The rotation instructions for 32-bit registers now rotate according to \reg_B instead of \reg_A in the shift count.
The rotation instructions for 32-bit registers now rotate according to \reg_B instead of \reg_A in the shift count.
The set used for indexing bits is changed from a power-of-two sized domain to 8n.

- Newly clarifies that if the RAM index is below 2^{16}, the machine panics.
- Also clarifies that if a memory region is not available for read/mutate, the machine faults at the “lowest inaccessible page address.”
Switched the notation to bold-math style for the block and header symbol.
In the call to \unzip_{684} , the argument went from (\mathbf{p}) to (\mathbf{d}).
A clarifying rewording to emphasize that the numbers are provisional.
The “input data” throughput changed from 2.5 MB/s and 852 MB/s to 2 MB/s and 682 MB/s.
The text now refers more simply to “32-bit account system” (instead of “4bn 32-bit”), and the example throughput was lowered from ~1.7 million TPS to ~1.4 million.
The “naive” throughput example changed from 15 MB & 90 KB to 12 MB & 48 KB, along with revised numbers for transactions and total TPS (previously: 3k transactions per package, or 312k tps in total).
The allowed output (“work result”) shrank from 90 KB to 48 KB.
“general-purpose I/O” changed from 2.5 mb/s to 2 mb/s.
Changed from 336 & 342
Renamed "Block publication" as "Authoring" and change previous values of 42 & 42.
Changed from 200 & 200
Changed from 60 & 56
Changed from 30 & 40
Changed 1tb to 8tb in the discussion about recommended hardware.
The literal text 3_500,000,000 (with underscore) changed to 3,500,000,000 (with a comma).

The symbol &\equiv changed to &\Leftrightarrow.
In context, R(...) is no longer just a definition/equivalence but an actual bidirectional logical condition.
Version was updated from 0.5.4 to 0.6.0 and "New Delhi" was added.
